question: access

request.from: a cloud container in a datacenter network, one IP
request.body: an MCP initialize request (jsonrpc 2.0, protocolVersion 2025-06-18, clientInfo public-agents-researcher 1.0), Content-Type application/json, Accept application/json and text/event-stream

decoded.challenge: www-authenticate: Bearer, resource_metadata="https://mcp.onfleet.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource" (the comma after the scheme is the record's, not the header's: the schema's credential rule refuses the verbatim value, and the transcript has it as sent); no realm, no scope, no error parameter
decoded.body: {"ok":false,"data":null,"error":{"code":"E_UNAUTHORIZED","message":"unauthorized"},"meta":{"request_id":...}} (the request id is a per-request UUID, left out here; the transcript has it as delivered)
decoded.protected-resource-metadata: 200 at the origin-level URL the challenge names (https://mcp.onfleet.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource, not the resource-specific /mcp path); resource https://mcp.onfleet.com (the origin, not the /mcp endpoint); authorization_servers: https://mcp.onfleet.com; bearer_methods_supported: header; no scopes_supported
decoded.authorization-server-metadata: 200 at https://mcp.onfleet.com/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server; issuer https://mcp.onfleet.com; registration and authorization endpoints on mcp.onfleet.com (oauth/register, oauth/authorize); token endpoint and jwks_uri on auth.us.prod.onfleet.com; response_types code; grants authorization_code, refresh_token; token auth none only; PKCE S256; no scopes_supported
decoded.rest: GET https://onfleet.com/api/v2/organization with no Authorization header answers 401 with code InvalidCredentials, error 1102, "The API key provided is invalid.", no www-authenticate; the error body echoes the caller's IP address and a request id

finding: With no credentials, an MCP initialize POST to mcp.onfleet.com/mcp answers 401 with a challenge naming a protected-resource document at the origin-level well-known path, and both metadata documents answer 200. The resource document names the origin, mcp.onfleet.com, as the resource rather than the /mcp endpoint, and names the same origin as its authorization server. That server publishes its registration and authorization endpoints on mcp.onfleet.com and its token endpoint and JWKS on a separate host, auth.us.prod.onfleet.com; it accepts public clients only (none is the sole token-auth method), requires PKCE S256, and lists no scopes in either document. The server is on no vendor page the entry cites (as of the 2026-09-14 read); this probe records what it publishes, not what the vendor intends. A keyless GET on the documented REST API answers 401 with the vendor's InvalidCredentials code and no challenge; the error body echoes the caller's IP. Same 401, discovery chain and REST status as the 2026-09-14 note; the origin-level resource id, the split token host and the absent scope lists are new here. Nothing here measures what either server does with a credential.
